name: base85n
description: Base85N: a compact encoding for data embedded in text formats

An encoding for data that has to live inside JSON, XML, HTML or a configuration file, where Base64 would otherwise be used. It uses a single 85-character alphabet that excludes every character those formats would force an escape for, so encoded output can be pasted verbatim, and adds two adaptive modes: Dynamic Passthrough, which carries text-like bytes at one character per byte, and Fill, which carries a run of up to 2048 identical bytes in five characters.
